questions.question: Who has the power to summon or prorogue a state legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** of a state is vested with the constitutional authority to **summon**, **prorogue**, and **dissolve** the state legislature under the provisions of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• According to **Article 174**, the **Governor** shall from time to time summon the House or each House of the State Legislature to meet at such time and place as they think fit.
 
• **Summoning** is the official process of calling the members of the **Legislative Assembly** or **Legislative Council** to commence a new session.
 
• **Prorogation** refers to the act of terminating a session of the House without dissolving the **Legislative Assembly** itself; it is typically done after a session is adjourned **sine die** by the presiding officer.
 
• The **Governor** must ensure that the maximum gap between two consecutive sessions of the state legislature does not exceed **six months**.
 
• While these powers are technically discretionary in certain extreme situations, the **Governor** generally exercises them based on the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speaker of the Assembly**:

 
 
• The **Speaker** has the power to **adjourn** the House, which means suspending the work in a sitting for a specific period (minutes, hours, or days).
 
• The **Speaker** can also adjourn the House **sine die**, which terminates a sitting for an indefinite period.
 
 
 
• **President of India**:
 
 
• Under **Article 85**, the **President** holds analogous powers at the central level to summon and prorogue the **Parliament** and dissolve the **Lok Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**:
 
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the state government who recommends the summoning or prorogation of the house to the **Governor**.
 
 
 
• **Dissolution**:
 
 
• While **prorogation** only ends a session, **dissolution** ends the very life of the **Legislative Assembly**, necessitating a fresh **General Election**.

questions.question: Who decides on disputes regarding the election of the Vice President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 71** of the **Constitution of India**, all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a **President** or **Vice-President** shall be inquired into and decided by the **Supreme Court**.
 
• The **Supreme Court** holds exclusive and original jurisdiction over such matters, and its decision is final and binding on all parties involved.
 
• An election petition challenging the election of the **Vice-President** can be presented to the **Supreme Court** only after the election process is concluded; it cannot be challenged while the election is in progress.
 
• If the **Supreme Court** declares the election of a person as **Vice-President** void, acts done by them in the exercise of their powers and duties before the date of the court's decision are not invalidated.
 
• The election of a **Vice-President** cannot be questioned on the ground of any vacancy existing among the members of the **Electoral College** electing them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India**:

 
 
• Under **Article 324**, the **Election Commission** is responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to the **Parliament**, **State Legislatures**, and the offices of **President** and **Vice-President**.
 
• While the **Election Commission** manages the procedural aspects of the election, it does not have the legal authority to adjudicate disputes regarding the validity of the election outcome.
 
 
 
• **Electoral College for Vice-President**:
 
 
• The **Vice-President** is elected by an **Electoral College** consisting of members of both Houses of **Parliament** (**Lok Sabha** and **Rajya Sabha**) through a system of **proportional representation** by means of a **single transferable vote**.
 
• This includes both **elected** and **nominated members** of **Parliament**, unlike the Presidential election where nominated members do not participate.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Role**:
 
 
• The **Vice-President** serves as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha** as per **Article 64** and **Article 89**.
 
• The term of office is **five years**, but the individual may continue to hold office until their successor enters upon the office.

questions.question: Maand, a semi-classical folk style, originates from which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maand** is a sophisticated **semi-classical** style of singing that originated in the **Marwar** region of **Rajasthan**, particularly associated with the **Jaisalmer** district.
 
• The name of this musical style is derived from **Maand**, which was the ancient geographical name for the **Jaisalmer** territory during the medieval period.
 
• It occupies a unique position in Indian music, bridging the gap between **Hindustani Classical** music and the **raw folk traditions** of the desert, characterized by its complex melodic structure.
 
• Historically, this style was patronized by the **royal courts** of **Rajasthan**, where professional singers performed for kings and nobles to celebrate **valour**, **romance**, and **seasonal changes**.
 
• The most iconic composition in this style is **Kesariya Balam Padharo Mare Desh**, which has become the definitive **cultural anthem** of the state, used to welcome tourists and dignitaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allah Jilai Bai**:

 
 
• She was a legendary **Maand singer** from **Bikaner** who gained international fame for her soulful renditions.
 
• In recognition of her immense contribution to the preservation of this art form, she was awarded the **Padma Shri** in **1982**.
 
 
 
• **Performers and Communities**:
 
 
• The preservation of **Maand** is largely credited to traditional musician communities such as the **Manganiyars** and **Langas**.
 
• Other notable exponents of this style include **Mangi Bai** of Udaipur and **Gavri Devi** of Jodhpur, both of whom specialized in royal court singing traditions.
 
 
 
• **Musical Attributes**:
 
 
• Unlike typical folk music, **Maand** requires formal training to master its **vocal modulations** and rhythmic patterns.
 
• It is often accompanied by traditional Rajasthani instruments like the **Kamayacha**, **Sarangi**, and **Khartal** to enhance the desert resonance.

questions.question: The minimum distance of the obstacle from the source of sound for a distinct echo is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17.2 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sensation of sound persists in the **human brain** for about **0.1 seconds**. This time interval is technically known as the **persistence of hearing**.
 
• To hear a **distinct echo**, the reflected sound must reach the ear after a time interval of at least **0.1 seconds** after the original sound is produced.
 
• The **speed of sound** in air at a standard room temperature (approximately **22 degrees Celsius**) is taken as **344 m/s**.
 
• The total distance traveled by the sound from the **source** to the **obstacle** and back to the listener is **2d**, where **d** represents the minimum distance of the obstacle.
 
• By applying the formula **Total Distance = Speed × Time**, we get **2d = 344 m/s × 0.1 s**, which equals **34.4 m**.
 
• The minimum distance **d** of the obstacle from the source is calculated by dividing the total distance by two: **34.4 m ÷ 2 = 17.2 m**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Echo:**

 
 
• **Temperature:** The speed of sound increases with an increase in **temperature**. Consequently, the minimum distance required for an echo also increases as the air gets warmer. For instance, at **0 degrees Celsius**, the speed is **331 m/s**, making the distance approximately **16.55 m**.
 
• **Medium:** Sound requires a **material medium** to travel. It travels fastest in **solids**, followed by liquids, and slowest in **gases**.
 
• **Reflecting Surface:** For an echo to be clear, the reflecting surface must be **large** enough compared to the wavelength of the sound and should be **rigid**.
 
 
 
• **Reverberation:**
 
 
• If the distance between the source and the obstacle is less than **17.2 m**, the reflections occur too quickly to be distinguished as separate sounds. This leads to the **persistence** or **prolongation** of sound, known as **reverberation**.

questions.question: The Northern Plains of India are primarily formed by the deposits of which type of soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Northern Plains of India** are a vast **depositional plain** formed over millions of years by the sediment loads of three major river systems: the **Indus**, the **Ganga**, and the **Brahmaputra**.
 
• As these Himalayan rivers flow from the mountains to the plains, they carry massive quantities of **silt**, **sand**, and **clay**, which are deposited in a large **foredeep** basin located at the foothills of the **Himalayas**.
 
• This continuous process of deposition has resulted in the formation of **Alluvial soil**, which covers about **40 percent** of India's total land area and makes the Northern Plains one of the most **fertile** agricultural tracts in the world.
 
• **Alluvial soil** is chemically rich in **potash**, **phosphoric acid**, and **lime**, although it is generally poor in nitrogen and organic matter.
 
• The soil is categorized into two types based on geological age: **Bhangar**, which is the older, less fertile alluvium containing calcareous deposits called **Kankar**, and **Khadar**, which is the newer, highly fertile alluvium replenished annually by floods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Soil**

 
 
• Commonly known as **Regur soil** or **Black Cotton Soil**, it is primarily found in the **Deccan Trap** region covering **Maharashtra**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Gujarat**.
 
• It is derived from the weathering of **basaltic rocks** (lava) and is known for its high **moisture-retention** capacity and self-plowing nature.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**
 
 
• This soil develops on **crystalline igneous rocks** in areas of low rainfall, such as the eastern and southern parts of the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• Its characteristic red color is due to the wide diffusion of **iron** in crystalline and metamorphic rocks; it appears yellow when found in a **hydrated** form.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil**
 
 
• Formed under conditions of **high temperature** and **heavy rainfall**, this soil is a result of intense **leaching** caused by tropical rains.
 
• It is rich in **iron oxide** and aluminum but poor in organic matter, making it suitable for **plantation crops** like **cashew nuts**, tea, and coffee.

questions.question: Which river creates the world's largest riverine island, Majuli?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Majuli** is officially recognized by the **Guinness World Records** as the largest river island in the world, located in the **Brahmaputra River** in the state of **Assam**, India.
 
• The island was formed due to the **Brahmaputra River** and its anabranch, the **Kherkutia Xuti**, joining with the **Subansiri River**, creating a unique mid-stream landmass.
 
• It is a significant center for **Neo-Vaishnavite** culture and philosophy, housing numerous **Sattras** (monastic institutions) established by the 15th-16th century saint-reformer **Srimanta Sankardev**.
 
• In **September 2016**, Majuli became the first island in India to be granted the status of a **district**, emphasizing its geographical and cultural importance to the nation.
 
• Despite its ecological richness, the island has faced severe **soil erosion**, shrinking from an estimated 1,250 square kilometers in the early 20th century to approximately 352 square kilometers today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmaputra River**

 
 
• Originates from the **Angsi Glacier** in the **Kailash Range** near **Mansarovar Lake** in Tibet, where it is known as the **Yarlung Tsangpo**.
 
• It enters India through **Arunachal Pradesh** as the **Siang** or **Dihang** river before flowing through the plains of **Assam**.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River**
 
 
• The largest river basin in India, originating from the **Gangotri Glacier** at **Gaumukh** in Uttarakhand, where it is known as the **Bhagirathi**.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River**
 
 
• Often referred to as the **Dakshin Ganga** or **Vriddha Ganga**, it is the longest river in **Peninsular India**, originating from **Trimbakeshwar** in Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna River**
 
 
• A major tributary of the Ganga, it originates from the **Yamunotri Glacier** on the **Bandarpunch peaks** of the **Lower Himalayas**.

questions.question: Which Indian youth athlete broke the 5000 m race walk national record by finishing in under 20 minutes (19:24.48)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitin Gupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nitin Gupta**, representing **Uttar Pradesh**, created a new national record in the **boys 5000 m race walk** at the **18th National Youth Athletics Championships**.
 
• He clocked an impressive time of **19:24.48**, becoming the first Indian youth athlete to break the **20-minute barrier** in this specific category.
 
• The event was held at the **MGM Stadium** in **Udupi, Karnataka**, in **March 2023**, which served as a selection trial for the **Asian Youth Athletics Championships**.
 
• Gupta shattered the previous national youth record of **20:11.84**, which was set by **Paramjeet Singh Bisht** in **2018**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)**:

 
 
• The **AFI** is the apex body for athletics in India and is responsible for conducting national championships and selecting athletes for international competitions like the **Olympics** and **Asian Games**.
 
 
 
• **Other Participants**:
 
 
• **Tushar Panwar**: He finished **second** in the same race with a time of **20:00.89**, also performing exceptionally well by nearly breaking the sub-20 minute mark and the previous record.
 
• **Yogita**: She is a notable **female race walker** who competed in the **girls 5000 m race walk** category during the same championships.
 
 
 
• **Race Walking Technique**:
 
 
• It is a specialized discipline where the athlete must always maintain **visible contact** with the ground and the **leading leg** must be straight from the point of contact until the vertical upright position.

questions.question: The Resolving Insolvency indicator evaluates:

options.text: Time, cost, and recovery rate in bankruptcy cases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Time, cost, and recovery rate in bankruptcy cases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Resolving Insolvency** indicator is a critical metric used to evaluate the efficiency of a country's **bankruptcy framework** and the legal infrastructure supporting the recovery of debts.
 
• It focuses on the **Recovery Rate**, which is calculated as cents on the dollar recovered by secured creditors through **reorganization**, **liquidation**, or **debt enforcement** proceedings.
 
• The **Time** component measures the duration (in calendar years) from the moment of a company's **default** until the point where creditors receive their final payment.
 
• The **Cost** component quantifies the total expenses involved in the insolvency proceedings, expressed as a percentage of the **debtor's estate value**, including **court fees**, **attorney fees**, and **liquidator fees**.
 
• The indicator also assesses the **Strength of Insolvency Framework Index**, which evaluates whether a country's laws follow international good practices for **insolvency proceedings**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ease of Doing Business (EoDB)**:

 
 
• This indicator was a fundamental part of the **World Bank's Ease of Doing Business** report, which ranked economies based on their regulatory environment.
 
• Effective **insolvency laws** are vital for a healthy **financial system** as they allow for the rapid reallocation of resources from failing firms to more productive ones.
 
 
 
• **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016**:
 
 
• In India, the **IBC** was introduced to streamline the insolvency process, significantly improving the **recovery rate** and reducing the **time** taken for resolution.
 
• The **National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)** is the designated adjudicating authority for handling corporate insolvency cases under this code.
 
• Before the **IBC**, insolvency resolution in India was governed by fragmented laws like the **SICA** and **SARFAESI Act**, which often led to prolonged delays.

questions.question: What is the planned purpose of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) unveiled by ISRO in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Space tourism and station support**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS)** is India's upcoming sovereign space station, conceptualized by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to establish a permanent human presence in **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
• As part of the expanded space roadmap unveiled by the Union Cabinet and **ISRO**, the station is designed to support a crew of **3 to 4 astronauts** for extended missions, facilitating long-term **station support** for various orbital operations.
 
• One of the strategic objectives of the **BAS** is to foster the commercialization of space, which includes providing infrastructure for **space tourism** and private sector participation in space-based activities.
 
• The facility will serve as a primary laboratory for **microgravity experiments** in fields such as biotechnology, materials science, and pharmaceutical research, providing a unique environment that cannot be replicated on Earth.
 
• The roadmap targets the launch of the first module, **BAS-1**, by **2028**, with the objective of making the entire multi-module station fully operational by the year **2035**.
 
• The station will utilize advanced **docking ports** compatible with the **Gaganyaan** crew module, ensuring seamless logistics and crew rotation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gaganyaan Program**:

 
 
• This is the foundational mission for **BAS**, aimed at demonstrating India's **Human Spaceflight Capability** by sending a crew to an altitude of 400 km.
 
• Successful execution of **Gaganyaan** is a prerequisite for the assembly and maintenance of the **Bharatiya Antariksh Station**.
 
 
 
• **Long-term Vision (Amrit Kaal)**:
 
 
• The **Indian Space Vision 2047** includes the establishment of the space station as a stepping stone toward a **manned lunar landing** by the year **2040**.
 
• It also focuses on the development of the **Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV)**, which will be capable of carrying heavier payloads required for station expansion.
 
 
 
• **Technological Features**:
 
 
• The station will incorporate an indigenous **Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS)** to sustain human life in the vacuum of space.
 
• It will act as a gateway for future deep-space exploration, providing a platform for **refueling** and equipment testing.

questions.solution:

questions.question: In which year did the Indian women's cricket team play its first-ever Test match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian women's cricket team** played its first-ever **Test match** in **1976**, marking the country's official entry into the longest format of the game for women.
 
• The historic match was played against the **West Indies** at the **M. Chinnaswamy Stadium** in **Bangalore** (now Bengaluru) starting on **October 31, 1976**.
 
• **Shantha Rangaswamy** led the side as the first **captain** of the Indian women's Test team during this debut series.
 
• The match was the opening fixture of a **six-match Test series** conducted across various venues in India during the **1976-77** season.
 
• While the inaugural Test ended in a **draw**, India achieved its first-ever **Test victory** in the fourth match of the same series, held at **Patna** in **November 1976**.
 
• The Indian squad featured pioneers such as **Fowzieh Khalili**, **Diana Edulji**, and **Shubhangi Kulkarni**, who played significant roles in establishing the foundation of women's cricket in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Women's Cricket Association of India (WCAI)**:

 
 
• Formed in **1973** by **Mahendra Kumar Sharma**, it was the primary governing body for women's cricket before merging with the **BCCI** in **2006**.
 
• The association was responsible for organizing the first **Inter-State Championship** in **1973** and securing international recognition for the Indian team.
 
 
 
• **Shantha Rangaswamy's Contributions**:
 
 
• She became the first Indian woman to score a **Test century**, which she achieved during the **1976** series against the **West Indies** at **Dunedin**.
 
• She was the first female cricketer to be honored with the **Arjuna Award** in **1976** and later received the **BCCI Lifetime Achievement Award**.
 
 
 
• **International Evolution**:
 
 
• Following their Test debut, India made its **One Day International (ODI)** debut in **1978** during the **Women's Cricket World Cup** hosted in India.
 
• The team's first **T20 International (T20I)** was played much later, in **2006**, against **England** at **Derby**.

questions.question: Who is known as the "Father of the White Revolution" in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Verghese Kurien**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dr. **Verghese Kurien** is celebrated as the **Father of the White Revolution** in India due to his pioneering role in **Operation Flood**, the world's largest dairy development program launched in **1970**.
 
• He transformed India from a milk-deficient nation into the **global leader in milk production**, overtaking the United States in **1998**.
 
• As the founder-chairman of the **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)**, he implemented the **Anand pattern** cooperative model, which eliminated middlemen and empowered millions of small-scale farmers.
 
• He was the driving force behind the **Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF)**, which manages the iconic brand **Amul**.
 
• For his extraordinary contributions to rural development and food security, he was honored with the **Ramon Magsaysay Award**, the **World Food Prize**, and India's second-highest civilian award, the **Padma Vibhushan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **M.S. Swaminathan**:

 
 
• Known as the **Father of the Green Revolution in India**.
 
• He introduced **high-yielding varieties (HYV)** of wheat and rice during the **1960s** to ensure national food security.
 
• He served as the Director General of the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)**.
 
 
 
• **Norman Borlaug**:
 
 
• Recognized as the **Father of the Green Revolution** globally.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize** in **1970** for developing semi-dwarf, disease-resistant wheat varieties that saved over a billion people from starvation.
 
 
 
• **Vikram Sarabhai**:
 
 
• Regarded as the **Father of the Indian Space Program**.
 
• He was the primary architect behind the establishment of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and the **Physical Research Laboratory (PRL)**.

questions.question: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into how many categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) of 1956** was adopted to replace the policy of 1948 and served as the **Economic Constitution of India** for several decades.
 
• It classified industries into **three distinct categories**, known as schedules, to define the respective roles of the **State** and **private enterprise**.
 
• **Schedule A** included **17 industries** which were the **exclusive responsibility of the State**; this included strategic sectors such as **arms and ammunition**, **atomic energy**, **iron and steel**, **heavy plant and machinery**, and **railways**.
 
• **Schedule B** consisted of **12 industries** that were to be progressively **State-owned**, but where **private enterprise** was expected to supplement the efforts of the State in establishing new units. This category included **aluminum**, **mining**, **machine tools**, and **fertilizers**.
 
• **Schedule C** comprised all the **remaining industries** not mentioned in the first two schedules, which were generally left open to the **private sector**, although they remained under the regulatory framework of the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Context and Framework:**

 
 
• The **IPR 1956** was the foundational pillar of the **Second Five-Year Plan**, which followed the **Mahalanobis Model** of development focusing on **heavy industries**.
 
• The policy aimed at achieving a **socialist pattern of society**, emphasizing the expansion of the **public sector** to reduce disparities in income and wealth.
 
• It introduced a strict **licensing system** for the private sector to promote **regional equality**, ensuring that industries were established in **economically backward regions** through tax concessions and subsidized power.
 
• The resolution also highlighted the importance of **village and small-scale industries** for providing employment and ensuring a decentralized **industrial structure**.

questions.question: Who was awarded the Knight's Cross of the Order of Dannebrog for strengthening Indo-Danish relations in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijay Sankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vijay Sankar**, the **Deputy Chairman** of the **Sanmar Group**, was conferred with the **Knight's Cross of the Order of Dannebrog** in **January 2025**.
 
• He has served as the **Honorary Consul General of Denmark** in **Chennai** since 2012, representing Danish interests in **Tamil Nadu**, **Kerala**, **Andhra Pradesh**, **Telangana**, and **Puducherry**.
 
• The honor was bestowed by **King Frederik X** of Denmark in recognition of Sankar's outstanding contribution to strengthening **bilateral ties** and fostering **economic cooperation** between **India** and **Denmark**.
 
• The award highlights his role in advancing the **Indo-Danish Green Strategic Partnership**, particularly in the areas of **renewable energy**, **shipping**, and **water technology**.
 
• This recognition is part of the **Danish Order of Chivalry**, which is awarded to individuals for significant service to Denmark's international relations or civil and military merit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Order of Dannebrog**:

 
 
• Established in **1671** by **King Christian V**, it is one of the most prestigious honors in the Danish honors system.
 
• The insignia features the **Dannebrog cross**, which reflects the **national flag of Denmark**.
 
 
 
• **Sanmar Group**:
 
 
• A prominent Indian conglomerate based in **Chennai** with a diversified presence in **chemicals**, **engineering**, and **shipping**.
 
• The group maintains long-standing industrial collaborations with several European partners, including Danish entities.
 
 
 
• **Natarajan Chandrasekaran**:
 
 
• The **Chairman** of **Tata Sons** who was awarded the **Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur** (Knight of the Legion of Honour) by France in 2023, but not the Danish honor in 2025.
 
 
 
• **Rajnath Singh**:
 
 
• The current **Minister of Defence** of India, who oversees **strategic defense partnerships** but was not the recipient of this specific diplomatic award.

questions.question: If the government adopts contractionary fiscal policy, it:

options.text: Reduces public expenditure or increases taxes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduces public expenditure or increases taxes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Contractionary Fiscal Policy** is a macroeconomic tool utilized by the **Government** to decrease the level of **Aggregate Demand** within an economy, primarily to control **inflation**.
 
• One of the fundamental mechanisms is the **reduction of public expenditure**, which involves cutting government spending on projects, services, and subsidies, thereby lowering the total amount of money circulating in the economy.
 
• Another critical component is **increasing taxes** (such as **Income Tax** or **Corporate Tax**), which reduces the **disposable income** of households and the **investment capacity** of businesses, leading to lower private consumption.
 
• This policy is typically implemented when an economy is **overheating**, where the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is growing too fast, leading to rising prices and an unsustainable **fiscal deficit**.
 
• The ultimate objective of these measures is to achieve **price stability** and prevent the erosion of **purchasing power** caused by excessive demand-pull inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Expansionary Fiscal Policy**:

 
 
• This is the opposite of contractionary policy, used during **recessions** to stimulate growth.
 
• It involves **increasing public expenditure** and **reducing taxes** to boost aggregate demand and reduce **unemployment**.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy vs. Fiscal Policy**:
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy** is managed by the **Ministry of Finance** through spending and taxation.
 
• **Monetary Policy** is managed by the **Central Bank** (such as the **RBI** in India or the **Federal Reserve** in the US) using tools like **interest rates** and **reserve ratios**.
 
• **Printing more money** is a form of **monetary expansion** (often called **deficit financing**), which is generally inflationary and contrary to contractionary goals.
 
 

Therefore, the correct option is 1

questions.question: Which segment of the Indian economy constitutes the second-largest source of employment after agriculture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME)** sector is widely recognized as the **engine of growth** for the Indian economy, serving as the largest employer after the **agriculture** sector.
 
• According to various government reports, including the **Ministry of MSME Annual Report**, the sector provides employment to approximately **11.10 crore** (111 million) people across **6.33 crore** unincorporated non-agriculture enterprises.
 
• This sector is characterized by its **labor-intensive** nature, allowing for a much higher employment-to-capital ratio compared to large-scale industrial units.
 
• MSMEs contribute roughly **30%** to India's **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** and account for nearly **45%** of the total **exports** from the country.
 
• The sector is crucial for **inclusive development** as it creates employment opportunities in **rural and semi-urban areas**, helping to reduce the migration of labor to metropolitan cities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Large-scale capital-intensive industrial enterprises**:

 
 
• These industries require heavy **financial investment** in machinery and technology. While they produce high value-added goods, their **direct employment generation** capacity is lower than MSMEs due to **automation**.
 
 
 
• **Information Technology and software services**:
 
 
• While the **IT-BPM** sector is a massive foreign exchange earner and employs approximately **5 million** professionals, its workforce is specialized and significantly smaller in volume compared to the MSME sector.
 
 
 
• **Classification Criteria**:
 
 
• Under the revised **MSME definition (2020)**, a **Micro** enterprise has investment ≤ 1 crore and turnover ≤ 5 crore; a **Small** enterprise has investment ≤ 10 crore and turnover ≤ 50 crore; and a **Medium** enterprise has investment ≤ 50 crore and turnover ≤ 250 crore.

questions.question: As of 1 March 2025, India has ___ crore active domestic LPG consumers, including 10.33 crore PMUY beneficiaries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**32.94**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **1 March 2025**, the total count of **active domestic LPG consumers** in India has reached a landmark figure of **32.94 crore**.
 
• This massive consumer base includes **10.33 crore beneficiaries** specifically enrolled under the **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)**, a flagship scheme aimed at providing clean energy to **economically weaker sections**.
 
• The expansion of LPG coverage is a key component of India's energy policy, overseen by the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**, to ensure the transition from traditional biomass to **Liquefied Petroleum Gas**.
 
• The achievement of **32.94 crore** connections signifies an almost universal access to clean cooking fuel across **rural and urban households** in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY):**

 
 
• Launched in **May 2016** from **Ballia, Uttar Pradesh**, with the objective of safeguarding the health of women and children by providing clean cooking fuel.
 
• The subsequent phase, **Ujjwala 2.0**, was introduced in **August 2021** to offer **deposit-free LPG connections** to migrants and low-income families who could not be covered in the first phase.
 
• The scheme provides a **targeted subsidy** of 300 rupees per cylinder to all **PMUY beneficiaries** to maintain affordability.
 
 
 
• **Operational Framework:**
 
 
• The supply and distribution are managed by **Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs)** such as **Indian Oil (IOCL)**, **Bharat Petroleum (BPCL)**, and **Hindustan Petroleum (HPCL)**.
 
• The **PAHAL (DBTL)** scheme ensures that **LPG subsidies** are transferred directly to the **Aadhaar-linked bank accounts** of consumers, minimizing diversion and ensuring transparency.

questions.question: Around which of the following years did the Santhals revolt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1855**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Santhal Rebellion**, also known as the **Santhal Hool**, was a major tribal uprising that took place in **1855-56** in the **Rajmahal Hills** of present-day **Jharkhand** and **West Bengal**.
 
• The revolt was led by four brothers: **Sidhu**, **Kanhu**, **Chand**, and **Bhairav** Murmu, who organized thousands of Santhals to fight against the British colonial authorities and their local collaborators.
 
• The primary cause of the rebellion was the oppressive **Zamindari system** and the **Permanent Settlement of 1793**, which led to the loss of tribal land and forced the Santhals into debt.
 
• The rebels targeted **moneylenders** (locally known as **Mahajans** or **Dikus**) and British officials who exploited the tribal population through exorbitant interest rates and land grabbing.
 
• The rebellion formally commenced on **June 30, 1855**, when a massive gathering at **Bhagnadih** declared independence from British rule and the zamindars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Reforms**:

 
 
• Following the suppression of the revolt, the British government created the **Santhal Parganas** district to ensure tribal laws were respected.
 
• The **Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act** was later enacted to protect the rights of the tribal population over their land and prevent transfers to non-tribals.
 
 
 
• **Damin-i-Koh**:
 
 
• This was a large area in the Rajmahal hills demarcated by the British in **1832** for the Santhals to settle and practice agriculture.
 
• Encroachment into this region by outsiders was a significant trigger for the **1855** uprising.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Years**:
 
 
• **1821**: This period saw early tribal unrest in Central India but does not coincide with the Santhal Hool.
 
• **1885**: This year is historically significant for the foundation of the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• **1903**: This era is associated with the aftermath of the **Munda Rebellion** (Ulgulan) led by **Birsa Munda**, which ended around 1900.
